$comment: Mainnet example of the company-wallet model (Talas 8.2) with placeholder public keys (fill-pattern addresses nobody holds). One company wallet holds the Super Admin (and its Admin record), the KYC registry authority, the BlocklistAuthority and the protocol treasury; acknowledgedRoleOverlaps names that key with its exact role set and a reason, without which the map is refused on mainnet. admins[] holds one more Admin record, a Ledger of another fully trusted person, so a lost company wallet does not also remove the pause; the program has no pause-only role, so that key has every Admin power (approve sales, clawback, custody, OTC): without it every tool warns NO SECOND ADMIN. The upgrade authority stays with the Squads vault (2 of 3, the company wallet is not a member). A 1-of-N vault needs "acknowledgedSingleKeyUpgradeAuthority": "<squads.multisig>" as well. The vault holds no operational role (v1.0.0-rc: SA, BA or an Admin record of the upgrade authority is a chain:inventory blocker). unpauseMask 35 (0x23: onboarding, primary issuance, issuer proceeds) is the pilot's first unpause: S6 leaves trading, custody entry and distributions paused (the pilot mask 0x1c) and the payout modules (0x40) off. Replace every key before use: kyc.registry = KycRegistry PDA(deployer); squads.vault = PDA([multisig, multisig, vault, 0], SQDS4). No secrets ever go in a role map. See ops/runbook-mainnet.md, Company wallet model.

acknowledgedRoleOverlaps.reason: Licensed operator (legal entity) holds every operational role in one company wallet until separate keys are staffed
